scenes.say: April 28, 1988. At 24,000 feet over Hawaii, the roof of Aloha Airlines Flight 243 tears away.

The skin overlapped at a lap joint, bonded and riveted. The bond let go, and the rivets carried the cabin pressure alone. Fatigue cracks grew at the rivet holes until they linked up, and the seam unzipped.

This airframe had flown 89,680 flights, and every one stretched that seam again. From line number 292, later 737s got an extra layer at this joint. This one, line 152, did not. Instead of stopping at a tear strap, the cracks joined up.
Thirteen minutes later, the crew landed on Maui. Sixty-five people were injured. Chief flight attendant Clarabelle Lansing was killed.

script.comment: Later 737s got an extra layer at this joint. Should the older airframes have flown without it?
